bullets.title: Tape in Freefall: QQQ -6%, SOXX -12%, VIX +45–65% intraday — worst since DeepSeek
bullets.body: Tech is the epicenter of a severe risk-off session: QQQ down ~6% (worst day since the DeepSeek shock, ~15% drawdown), SOXX down 12% at the lows (~40% drawdown matching COVID and 2022 tech recession levels), and VIX spiking 45–65% intraday — the largest single-day move in two years. S&P 500 is down 2.9% to ~7,468. MegaCap Tech is down 415bps and providing no support; TMT broadly down 9.5% (-2 standard deviations).

bullets.title: Election blue sweep drives AI power/data-center selloff; hyperscalers outperform on relative safety
bullets.body: Democratic midterm sweep — including a Texas gubernatorial win — triggered the AI power basket to fall 10.4% (CEG -6.7%, VST -13.8%), data center infrastructure stocks lower, and neocloud/compute plays hardest hit. Hyperscalers (META, MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL) are outperforming the wreckage, with CDS spreads tightening, as markets read a blue sweep as potentially constraining frontier AI regulation at the federal level but raising data-center permitting risk at the state level. 278 stocks hit 52-week highs vs. 184 at 52-week lows, with Electronic Technology showing 2 highs vs. 30 lows.

bullets.title: Texas regulatory risk now a real threat to AI infrastructure delivery timelines and financing
bullets.body: Post-election analysis flags that Texas's regulatory outcome creates counterparty delivery risk on major AI data center projects, with complex multi-party contracts between compute offtakers and power offtakers now under heightened scrutiny on deliverability dates. Buyers of data center services are likely to slow decisioning and shift demand toward states with clearer power grid certainty. Key unknowns: 2027–2028 GW capacity delivery, hyperscaler capex alignment, and AI revenue strength justifying further capex.

bullets.title: Microsoft turns negative on neocloud partnerships; capex cuts tied to Iren/Nscale delays
bullets.body: Microsoft leadership is increasingly negative on neocloud data center developers, citing project delays, regulatory headwinds, and rising costs. MSFT increased oversight of partnerships with Iren, Nebius, and Nscale, declined an option to expand its Nscale agreement, and its Q1 lower capex is directly attributable to Iren project delays. IREN is down 71.3% from its 52-week high.

bullets.title: Wolfe fades post-election narratives: semis selloff overdone, clean energy gains unlikely, tariff relief narrow
bullets.body: Wolfe Research argues the semis selloff is overdone — state-level data-center moratoria impose conditions but won't stop existing pipeline projects. Clean energy IRA credit reversal is off the table. Tariff relief on Canada/Mexico is likely but USMCA-specific only, and Congressional override of Trump veto authority is a non-starter. A healthcare deal is plausible in 2027 but requires a debt-ceiling catalyst, arriving late in the year.

bullets.title: Flow data: 2:1 buy-to-sell overall but LOs dumping Tech; Growth underperforms Value by 320bps (3-sigma move)
bullets.body: Desk volumes are running +100% vs. Wednesday at the same time and +65% vs. the 10-day average. Despite a headline 2:1 buy-to-sell ratio, Long Only supply is concentrated in Tech and Industrials; hedge funds are heavily shorting Communications Services (65% of HF sales). Growth is underperforming Value by 320bps — a 3-standard-deviation relative move. Defensives are outperforming Cyclicals by 225bps, and Russell 2000 is outperforming Nasdaq by 365bps.

bullets.title: LO flows now dominate Tech selling (55% of notional); Tech vs. S&P in oversold territory for first time since Iran escalation
bullets.body: Long-only flows account for 55% of notional selling in Tech vs. hedge funds at 45% — a flip from prior violent AI reactions where HFs led. Tech vs. the S&P 500 is now in oversold territory for the first time since the Iran war escalation. Utilities is the only net-buy subsector, reflecting a defensive/low-beta positioning rotation.

bullets.title: Citi quant cycle model flips bearish on stocks; US market >2 std devs above long-term trend
bullets.body: Citi's market-cycle model reversed to bearish after the AI-linked pullback, with the US market trading more than two standard deviations above its long-term trend — a statistically rare maturity signal. The firm's house view counters that financing strain is concentrated in weaker balance sheets, chip rental prices remain firm, and AI demand from robotics and self-improving agents is still accelerating. Global 10-year yields are up 175bps in France and 100+ bps in the US and UK since the Iran conflict began; 16 of 27 major central banks are expected to raise rates this year.

bullets.title: 3Q earnings solid but momentum cooling: beats declining, Tech/Comms facing rotation headwinds
bullets.body: S&P 1500 earnings and sales beats remain above long-term medians but declined from 2Q (earnings -4.8pp, sales -8pp), with nine sectors posting smaller beats. S&P y/y earnings growth stands at 27.9%, but the share of companies growing earnings >20% has stalled. Tech and Communications retain the strongest growth distributions but posted negative excess returns even after earnings beats, as AI-driven rotation weighs on multiples.

bullets.title: US productivity strong at 3.6% q/q but unit nonlabor costs surging 5.2% q/q; inflation sticky into 1H27
bullets.body: Nonfarm business productivity jumped 3.6% q/q (a.r.) in 3Q26, well above the 2.7% consensus, but the y/y pace of 2.1% trails 2024–2025 trends. Unit nonlabor costs surged 5.2% q/q a.r. and 6.0% y/y, driven by oil, tariffs, and AI demand. Initial jobless claims fell to 189k — the lowest since 1969 — but upward revisions to labor and nonlabor costs underline pass-through risks to above-target consumer inflation, expected to remain sticky through 1H 2027.

bullets.title: BoE hikes 25bps, signals 1–2 more; upgraded GDP to 1.6%, cut unemployment forecast to 5.0%
bullets.body: The BoE voted 8-1 to hike 25bps in November with hawkish forward guidance. Governor Bailey indicated hikes will continue unless the Middle East conflict resolves, explicitly contradicting an energy-only narrative. The BoE upgraded 2026 GDP growth from 1.1% to 1.6% and cut its end-2027 unemployment projection from 5.3% to 5.0%, making a slack-driven disinflation argument harder to sustain. February remains the base case for the next hike but December is live, with at least three hawkish MPC members (Greene, Pill, Mann) supportive.

bullets.title: HF prime update: TMT severely down Nov 5; semis-to-software rotation hammered US momentum Nov 4
bullets.body: On November 4, a semis-to-software rotation caused a sharp US momentum sell-off even as broader markets rose; systematic L/S ended slightly up on EM Asia offsets. November 5 sees US markets in full sell-off mode — TMT severely down, fundamentals funds hit harder than US-focused peers, and multi-strategy funds down significantly on equity exposure. Systematics are positive on the day.

bullets.title: JPM GBI-EM adds Philippines and Saudi Arabia Jan 2027; country caps cut from 10% to 9%
bullets.body: Philippines Peso government bonds (1.64% terminal weight) and Saudi Riyal Sukuk (2.71% terminal weight) will phase into the GBI-EM GD index starting January 29, 2027, over a 10-month period. Country weight caps for all nations are simultaneously reduced from 10% to 9%, with China, India, and Mexico seeing the largest reductions. EMEA exposure shifts to 29.5% from 27.3%; Asia exposure declines ~1%.

bullets.title: QCOM down 12% pre-market: handset miss, 330bps QCT margin guide miss, DC ramp costs bite
bullets.body: QCOM's Q4 beat on revenue (+3.2%) but gross margin came in 250bps below consensus at 50.8%, driven by data center ramp expenses and broad input cost inflation. Q1 QCT EBT margin guidance of 20–22% missed FactSet at 24.3% by 330bps. Management targets $650M+ DC revenue in Q1 and a $15B+ DC run-rate by FY29, but sell-side is skeptical given intense competition and dilutive near-term margins. Stock is down ~12% pre-market.

bullets.title: AI infrastructure 'generals' failing at margins; weaker balance sheets can't finish buildouts, making compute scarcer
bullets.body: Citi flags that AI infrastructure market leaders are beginning to miss at the margin level — a potential signal for calling a cycle top. Weaker balance sheets are failing to complete data-center buildouts, which paradoxically makes compute scarcer and could benefit those with stronger balance sheets still able to borrow freely. Global AI capex is projected to exceed $3.5 trillion by 2030, competing directly with sovereign debt for savings.

bullets.title: El Niño forming with sea temps 3°C above normal; food price shock risk in ~6 months
bullets.body: A record El Niño is forming with sea surface temperatures now 3°C above normal and rising toward 3.5–4°C. India's monsoon is 30–40% below normal, flipping the country from a sugar exporter to importer. Food-price shocks typically take ~6 months to reach consumer inflation, putting the risk window in Q1–Q2 2027 and adding to already-sticky nonlabor cost pressures.

bullets.title: AMAT: Citi Buy ahead of 11/12 print; supply chain constraints a peer problem, not AMAT's
bullets.body: Citi maintains Buy on AMAT with a $710 PT (92% upside) ahead of its October-quarter report on November 12. Semi-cap peers are struggling with component shortages (MFC, IC, PCB, DRAM, MLCC), but AMAT's scale, diversified portfolio, and >2x manufacturing capacity expansion should enable superior supply-chain management. Citi forecasts $224B/$286B WFE in CY27/28 and targets >200bps WFE share gains for AMAT by CY30, with HBM revenue >$1B in CY26 at 60%+ market share.

bullets.title: Marvell/Lumentum merger: compelling strategic logic as optics-silicon convergence accelerates
bullets.body: Raymond James sees strong industrial logic in the Marvell/Lumentum deal, as NPO and CPO become critical for connecting accelerators and switches. Marvell brings DSPs, SerDes, and custom silicon; Lumentum adds lasers, optical components, and photonic manufacturing. Optical component margins have improved on scarcity and industry consolidation, not just cycle dynamics, and the convergence of optics and silicon makes this merger more attractive than it would have been in prior years.

bullets.title: CSCO downgraded to Equal-Weight; re-rating played out, lower-margin AI mix limits upside
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley downgraded Cisco to Equal-Weight from Overweight, citing that the re-rating thesis has played out and lower-margin AI product mix reduces the probability of positive earnings surprises. This follows a broader theme of AI mix pressure on margins across the sector.

bullets.title: Front-office software hit by top-of-funnel pressure; HUBS guide slashed, FIG AI consumption surging
bullets.body: Citi's 3Q26 front-office software recap shows top-of-funnel headwinds: HubSpot added only 5,258 net new customers (vs. 10,900 y/y), cut Q4 revenue guidance by $18M vs. consensus, and saw Citi's PT cut to $230 from $287. Figma is the standout — AI consumption up 2.5x since its October Agent GA launch, contributing 6 points of revenue growth, with revenue +43% y/y and Q4 guidance $13M above consensus.
